blocks.text: The molecular orbital approach explains the results of quantum mechanical calculations for covalent bonding. Its postulates are as follows.

items: During the formation of a molecule the atomic orbitals of the combining atoms overlap to form new orbitals called molecular orbitals, which belong to the whole molecule.
The atomic orbitals overlap with the lobe having the suitable sign of the wave function; one lobe of a p orbital is given the + sign and the other the - sign.

Two atomic orbitals overlap to form two molecular orbitals. When orbitals of the same sign overlap, a bonding molecular orbital (sigma or pi) forms, with lower energy than the parent atomic orbitals; with opposite signs a high-energy antibonding molecular orbital (sigma* or pi*) forms, with higher energy than the parent atomic orbitals.

The number of bonds between two atoms after the overlap is the bond order, taken as half the difference between the number of bonding electrons (a) and antibonding electrons (b): bond order = (a - b) / 2.

blocks.text: In the formation of H2 two s orbitals combine to give two molecular orbitals. The bonding molecular orbital sigma 1s is symmetrical about the axis joining the nuclei (the nuclear axis), while the antibonding orbital sigma* 1s has its electron density away from the nuclei of the overlapping atoms.

blocks.alt: (a) Energy Diagram: an upward Energy arrow; H 1s on the left and right, each with one electron; above, sigma* 1s (empty) and below, sigma 1s with a pair of opposite arrows for H2. (b) Electron Probability Distribution: MO2, sigma* 1s antibonding molecular orbital, two separate lobes around the two nuclei; MO1, sigma 1s bonding molecular orbital, one oval enclosing both nuclei.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.34: Formation of bonding and anti-bonding orbitals for the H2 molecule (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.34).

blocks.text: Head-on approach: the p orbitals of the two atoms approach along the same axis (say the x axis), giving the sigma 2px bonding and sigma* 2px antibonding molecular orbitals. Sideways approach: when the axes of two p orbitals (py or pz) are parallel they interact to form pi molecular orbitals. The bonding orbitals pi 2py and pi 2pz have zero electron density on the nuclear axis, which is a nodal plane, while the antibonding pi* 2py and pi* 2pz have the least electron density in the internuclear region.

blocks.alt: Six panels with + and - signs on the lobes. 2py - 2py gives an antibonding pi2p* with four lobes and a dotted node; 2py + 2py gives a bonding pi2p, one cloud above (+) and one below (-). 2pz - 2pz gives an antibonding pi2p*; 2pz + 2pz gives a bonding pi2p. 2px + 2px gives an antibonding sigma*2p with a node between the nuclei; 2px - 2px gives a bonding sigma2p with one large + region between the nuclei.
